caption:
Global Metadata: An epic cinematic fantasy battle anthem, 120 BPM, bold A minor with heroic lifts. The piece opens with a lone piano over hushed strings and a low timpani rumble, builds into a confident verse, erupts in a full brass-and-drums heroic chorus, drops to a pure instrumental interlude, then climbs to a final soaring chorus and a big orchestral fade-out. Instrumentation is deliberately Western and solid: grand piano, full string section, heroic brass fanfare (trumpets and horns), timpani and driving drums, electric bass, and warm cello. Strictly NO wind instruments (no flute, no dizi, no reeds, no woodwinds), NO harp, and NO plucked-string instruments anywhere. Every note has a clean, definite attack — no breath noise, no airy hiss, no glassy ringing — crisp modern studio production, wide cinematic stereo, deep tight low end. Production profile: high-budget film-score anthem, resplendent brass, punchy drums, studio mastering with generous dynamic range.

Vocal Details: One lead voice with a fixed identity and timbre held consistent through the whole song. A powerful, clear male tenor singing in Mandarin Chinese, natural and unforced, no auto-tune, warm and grounded with a strong confident tone. In the choruses he is joined by a supporting male choir (a blended men's chorus) for sheer power, but the lead tenor always stays clearly on top. No child vocals, no female vocals, no falsetto. No spoken dialogue anywhere. The lead voice never swaps or drifts.

Arrangement: Intro, a lone piano picking a quiet heroic motif over hushed low strings and a distant timpani rumble, very clean, no other instruments. Verse one, the piano continues, warm strings swell underneath, soft cello answers the lead tenor, the drums begin a steady confident pulse. Verse two, strings take the lead, brass enters gently, the drive strengthens. Chorus one, the full orchestra opens up, heroic brass fanfare, driving drums and timpani, a powerful male choir backs the lead tenor, the triumphant peak. Final chorus, bigger and higher, more brass and percussion, the peak of the whole piece. Interlude and outro are pure instrumental: piano and brass build over rolling drums, then a big full-orchestra fade-out on a resonant final chord. Every section is built on clean, definite instrument attacks.
lyrics:
[Intro]
No vocals. A lone piano over hushed low strings and a distant timpani rumble
clean and pure, instrumental only

[Verse 1]
黎明之前 心跳如鼓
we rise to answer the call
forged in steel, we run
迎着风 我们向前

[Chorus]
Lift your voice, let the thunder ring!
steel and brass, the banners swing
we will not bow, we sing
直到天地为我们回响

[Interlude]
No vocals. Piano and brass build over rolling drums and strings
pure instrumental interlude, no singing

[Verse 2]
Through the ash, through the flame
we walk the long road again
穿过星火 走向光
the night is ours to claim

[Final Chorus]
Rise and roar, the world is ours!
drums of war and rising towers
never once, we'll falter now
让每颗心 烧成骄阳

[Outro]
No vocals. Full orchestra, piano and brass and timpani
fading on a resonant final chord, instrumental only
